$comment: COMMON + SPECIALISATIONS. v1 took common plus one HOST tier, which is too coarse: a template like
spring + mongoose is Spring-authored AND Mongoose-hosted, and the skills that differ by authoring
style are not the ones that differ by host.
The shape states the rule: `common` is a list and is always selected; `specialisations` is a map and a
TEMPLATE names the ones it wants. Selection = common + the named specialisations. There is deliberately
no classification of a specialisation as host-or-style — nothing selects on that.
REPLAY IS A SPECIALISATION, NOT COMMON (review F3). replay-a-run carries a required TODO(bundle) marker
and the accepted M19 bundle has no replay entry point, so making it unconditional would either trip the
fail-on-TODO bundle gate or ship a fictional procedure. Only a template with a real replay entry point
selects it.
'spring' means the same here as appliesTo:'spring' in reference-set.json.
substitutes every marker and passes that gate on a generated bundle. Until then v1 remains the
There is deliberately NO `templates` map here. A template declares the specialisations it wants, and
templates are the playground's catalogue — centralising one of them in this analyser-owned index would
be the second source of truth this design exists to avoid. A sample selection lives in a TEST FIXTURE
instead (CanonicalSkillsTest), which exercises the rule without owning the data.
consumer must reproduce what it advertises. This draft deliberately declares NEITHER: an unpinned draft
PUBLISHED 2026-08-30. A playground generator consumed this end to end and deployed a bundle from it, so
the DRAFT status is lifted and the provenance guarantee now binds: this index pins the revision that
contains every selected byte, plus a per-path sha256. CanonicalSkillsTest enforces both, and refuses a
non-DRAFT index that pins nothing.

RE-PINNED 2026-09-16: load-audit-log, run-mongoose-server and add-a-node learned from an agent's session report on the 1.13.0 bundle (see CHANGELOG). Same contract, same selection; only the revision and the three hashes moved. Bundles generated from the earlier revision keep their own pinned bytes.
RE-PINNED 2026-09-16 (second time): add-a-node and run-mongoose-server reworded after the 1.13.1 independent review; same contract, same selection.

RE-PINNED 2026-09-17: guided-start spotlights before each beat speaks (M64.5). Same contract, same selection; only the revision and the guided-start hash moved. The pinned revision was made on a feature branch - if that branch is ever rebased, this revision must be re-pinned to the rewritten commit.

RE-PINNED 2026-09-17 (after the rebase onto main): the branch WAS rebased, so the commit above was rewritten; the revision now names the rewritten one, which is an ancestor of main. Same bytes, same hashes. CanonicalSkillsTest had stayed green locally against the OLD revision only because its commit object was still in the clone - it would have been red on CI.

RE-PINNED 2026-09-17 (M64.8 + M64.9, one edit): THE SELECTION GREW BY ONE. `common` gains point-at-the-fault - the shape of a fault-finding runbook that ends by spotlighting the evidence it matched - so every template now selects it; additive, same contract, and a generator that copies `common` needs no change. guided-start changed by one line: the spotlight target that lights the Topology tab's verdict line is `topology:verdict` (it was `coverage`, which misnamed what it lights). Bundles generated from an earlier revision keep their own pinned bytes; the playground must re-vendor to pick these up.

RE-PINNED 2026-09-21: point-at-the-fault gains a write-up section - the symptom evidenced by the cited record, the cause by the fix diff and before/after copies of the changed sources, source-only claims labelled, a pack that stands alone - after blind second readers of A3 reports could verify the symptom but not a code-level cause. Same contract, same selection; only the revision and this one hash moved. The playground must re-vendor to pick it up. (The revision is the description-length fix, one commit after the section itself.)

RE-PINNED 2026-09-21 (second time): point-at-the-fault is routed to by the bundle and says what a fixer must keep (evidence first, no regeneration for a body change, no data edits, read an edge-triggered flag); add-a-node asks authors to log the state behind a decision. Tested on Haiku A3 before release (3 of 3 loaded the skill, kept evidence, fixed byte-identically). Same contract, same selection; the revision and two hashes moved. The playground must re-vendor.
RE-PINNED after tool-agreement review: combined main point-at-the-fault/add-a-node and corrected Mongoose guidance; this revision contains every selected byte.

mongoose.why: the processor is hosted by a Mongoose server

embedded.why: the processor runs in-process via DataFlowConnector

spring.why: the graph is authored as Spring XML and compiled ahead of time

replay.why: the project has a REAL replay entry point the bundle can name; without one, replay-a-run's TODO(bundle) cannot be substituted
